name: Mushroom Reef Marine Sanctuary
signature: A protected rock platform reef teeming with marine life — the Peninsula's best low-tide snorkel and rock pool exploration
editorNote:
Mushroom Reef Marine Sanctuary is a protected intertidal reef east of Flinders — a series of basalt rock platforms exposed at low tide that contain some of the richest rock pool life on the entire Peninsula. Sea stars, anemones, blennies, octopus, and the occasional weedy sea dragon make it a genuine discovery zone for anyone willing to get their feet wet.

The reef is also a snorkelling spot at higher tides — the water clarity is excellent and the protected status means the marine life is far more abundant and less skittish than at unprotected reefs. Bring a mask and take time.

Access is via a short walk from the Flinders Blowhole carpark. Time your visit to low tide — check the Bureau of Meteorology tide chart before you go. No collecting, no touching — look only.
whyWeGo: The best rock pool and snorkel experience on the Peninsula — protected, rich, and completely free.
ifOnlyOneThing: Check the tide chart and arrive 30 minutes before low tide. The pools are best when the reef is freshly exposed.
